changes.before: New or expanded stand-alone data center or battery energy storage system land-use applications submitted after July 27, 2026; does not affect applications already under review.
changes.after: New or expanded data centers and battery energy storage systems as primary uses, as defined by Resolution No. 2932, including qualifying uses that are not stand-alone. Applications submitted before the moratorium may continue.
changes.reason: The signed resolution defines primary use by several site-level criteria; stand-alone is too narrow.

changes.before: Active as of the July 31, 2026 research date. Effective immediately upon adoption, the resolution bars submission, acceptance, processing, or approval of new land-use applications for new or expanded data centers or battery energy storage systems as primary uses. Applications already under review are not affected. Runs 120 days (to approximately 2026-11-24) absent extension or repeal, with council review required before expiration.
changes.after: Resolution 2932 defines primary use by alternative site-level floor-area, construction-cost and electrical-capacity criteria; a site may have multiple primary uses. The city says pre-moratorium applications may continue. This corrects the overly narrow stand-alone description; actual later extensions/repeal and legal force remain unresolved. changes.before: Moratorium ordinance adopted by the Woodburn City Council on 2026-09-14; the city filed the required 45-day notice of intent to consider a moratorium with the Oregon Department of Land Conservation and Development on 2026-07-30 before the council could act.
changes.after: Resolution No. 2267, adopted by Woodburn City Council on September 14, 2026 under ORS 197.505–540. The city filed a 45-day notice with the Oregon Department of Land Conservation and Development.
changes.reason: The city identifies Resolution 2267 rather than an ordinance, and filed a notice.

changes.before: Active as of 2026-09-23. Moratorium prevents city planning staff from considering any new data center land-use application, effective 2026-09-14 through 2027-01-12. Adopted after the city learned that data center developer Verrus (which had separately applied to build in Salem, where its application drew significant public resistance) was exploring development of a data center on a 237-acre privately owned Southwest Industrial Reserve Area parcel brought into Woodburn's urban growth boundary in 2025; Woodburn had not received a formal application as of adoption. The city separately adopted an ordinance in June 2026 designating data centers as a conditional use in that industrial reserve area, and has hired a consultant (Thomas Consulting Group) to help review and potentially revise its development code for data centers.
changes.after: The city identifies September 14 adoption of Resolution 2267, not an ordinance. Section 3 states immediate effectiveness upon adoption for 120 calendar days unless extended or repealed; Exhibit A reports July 30 notice to DLCD. Actual later action, operative interval and current legal force remain unresolved. [VERIFY: operative interval, later amendments/extensions/repeal, judicial developments and current legal force.]
